_doc: cinema.sc rooms. One entry per screening room; every number the app needs lives here (the .sc is generic).
Copy this whole cinema.data.example/ folder to server/world/scripts/cinema.data/ and edit the numbers for your
own room (they were built for a 7x7x11 test room near 0,-60,0 — see cinema-and-gallery.md Step 3 for how to
verify each position live before trusting it, and Step 8 for the full worked example this room is taken from).
YAW CONVENTION (verify it once on your own wall — pick a quad, view it from one known side, adjust, then reuse):
yaw = the direction the VIEWERS stand in, as a Minecraft yaw: 0 = viewers south (+z), -90 = viewers east (+x),
90 = viewers west (-x), 180 = viewers north (-z). The same value works for text_display (yaw 0 is readable
from the south) and for the mannequin (Rotation yaw = the way it looks).
POSITIONS: entity pos = the quad's centre, 0.05 in front of the wall FACE, never inside the wall block (a wall
block at integer z=Z spans Z..Z+1 — the face the room's interior sees is whichever side faces the room).
SEATS: [x, y_seat, z] where y_seat is the y of the seat block (e.g. a stair). The invisible Marker armor_stand
is spawned at y_seat + seat_dy; a Marker stand's rider sits with feet at stand y - 0.6, so seat_dy 0.5 puts
the feet at y_seat - 0.1 (measured live — see cinema-and-gallery.md, 'Seats').
LIGHTS: every `light` block inside the lights box is set to level `dim` during a film and back to `on` after.
sound.pos / sound.volume feed scarpet sound(music, pos, volume, 1, 'record'); volume > 1 only extends the range.
BUTTON: a plain vanilla button block. button.block = its cell, button.state = the block state the app places
if the cell holds no button; button.label/label_pos = a small text_display above it. Pressing it (powered
rising edge, polled every 2 ticks) opens the programme dialog for the nearest real player within 5 blocks,
3 s cooldown per player. A ticket-seller NPC (click), if you add one, opens the same dialog.
